headline: AMD unveils Threadripper Halo Station, an AI workstation with 96 cores and dual liquid-cooled MI350P accelerators
summary: Dubbed 'the most powerful workstation in the world,' AMD's new Threadripper Halo Station can run trillion-parameter AI models. It's expected to cost upwards of $100,000.
details: AMD announced the Threadripper Halo Station at IFA 2026, claiming it's "the most powerful workstation in the world." It features a 96-core Threadripper Pro 9995WX CPU and dual liquid-cooled Instinct MI350P accelerators. AMD states it can run trillion-parameter AI models.

The machine is expected to have a street price exceeding $100,000 for core components, potentially climbing over $150,000 with additional storage, power, and cooling. This high cost reflects its server-grade capabilities.

Essentially a server tray reconfigured into a tower, the system replaces an EPYC host with the 96-core Threadripper. AMD shared limited details beyond specs, indicating it's a system design for OEM partners to build and ship, though no partners have been announced yet.

At its core, the Threadripper Pro 9995WX is a 96-core, 192-thread Zen 5 chip, boosting up to 5.4 GHz. It comes with 384 MB of L3 cache and a 350W TDP, with standalone chips estimated around $11,000-$12,000.

The MI350P accelerators are built on TSMC N3 with 128 CDNA 4 compute units. Each accelerator includes 144GB of HBM3E memory, providing 288GB total, with potential for two more accelerators to reach 576GB HBM3E.
These powerful GPUs demand significant power, with each MI350P rated for up to 600W. While AMD doesn't sell them through consumer channels, each accelerator is estimated to cost around $20,000.
The system also includes 2TB of DDR5 memory, the maximum supported by the Threadripper Pro 9995WX's eight-channel configuration. This amount of DDR5 currently costs approximately $50,000.

AMD has not yet set an official price or release date for the Threadripper Halo Station. Further details are expected from AMD's OEM partners in the near future, with similar high-end workstations like the Lenovo ThinkStation P8 reaching over $330,000.
